summary: Repaired node1’s control script. It now safely handles live, stale, missing, and foreign PIDs, uses the available Python 3 runtime, serializes concurrent actions, preserves the journal, and is healthy after reboot with one worker running.
actions_performed: Replaced presence-only PID handling with process identity validation.
Added serialized start/stop/status actions using flock.
Made repeated and concurrent starts idempotent.
Ensured stop never signals a foreign process.
Validated recovery from the actual stale PID left by a node reboot.
Preserved AlmaLinux 9.6, kernel 5.14, and the existing journal record.

evidence.requirement: Live, stale, and foreign PID handling
evidence.summary: Commands demonstrate stale recovery, live status/stop, foreign-PID identification, stale status, and clean stopped status.

evidence.requirement: Repeated starts retain exactly one worker
evidence.summary: Sequential starts retained the same PID; five concurrent starts produced exactly one worker.
A foreign sleep process remained alive after foreign-PID stop, replacement start, and subsequent worker stop.
The original 'previous worker completed batch B100' record remained at line 1 before and after reboot; journal data continued appending.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel preserved

evidence.summary: Healthy baseline used boot ID dfdea52d-a1af-4d7b-803a-15f40ee9dd4e; reboot was acknowledged; node returned with boot ID ac1f17df-2198-455e-9569-2993b2250197; the leftover PID was detected as stale and recovery produced one healthy worker with preserved data and configuration.
